name: Lost Cities
edition: The Original Card Game, base game with 5 expeditions, 2018 Thames & Kosmos rulebook

source.title: Lost Cities: The Original Card Game manual (2018)

setup.text: Put the board between the players with the base game side up (five discard spaces).
Box the 12 purple cards (9 expedition and 3 wager). Shuffle the other 60.
Have pen and paper ready to tally scores.
Shuffle the 60 cards, deal 8 face down to each player, and put the rest face down as the draw pile beside the board.
The oldest player begins, then you alternate. In later games the player with the most points starts.

turn.summary: Play one card, then draw one card.
steps: Play a card by either adding it to one of your expedition columns on your side of the board, or discarding it on the pile of its colour.
Each new card in a column must be higher than the last card you placed there. Overlap cards so every number shows.
Wager cards go only at the start of a column, and several may be stacked there.
Then draw the top card of the draw pile, or the top card of any discard pile.

end: The game ends as soon as a player draws the last card from the draw pile. Score both players, then repeat for three games in total.

scoring.text: For each column, add the card values and subtract 20. A colour with no cards placed scores nothing.
One, two or three wager cards multiply that result by 2, 3 or 4.
A column of 8 or more cards earns a 20 point bonus.
Add the column totals together. After three games the highest overall score wins.

missed.text: You must play a card before you draw. Passing is not allowed.
You cannot draw the card you just discarded.
Once you place a number card in a column, you can no longer add wager cards to it.
The 20 point bonus is not multiplied by wager cards.
A column can score negative, and wagers multiply a negative result too.
Cards you discard go to the pile of their colour, not to a pile of your choice.

not_covered: Long game with six expeditions (only mentioned briefly)
Four-player and solo rules are separate downloads
